course_name: Algorithms and Data Structures - 2. Data Structures

course_profile.one_sentence_summary: A core computer science course focusing on the rigorous mathematical analysis, design, and practical implementation of advanced data structures and algorithmic strategies.
course_profile.short_summary: This course covers foundational and advanced algorithmic techniques, including divide and conquer, dynamic programming, and greedy algorithms. It extensively studies complex data structures such as hash tables, binary search trees, red-black trees, and priority queues, culminating in a theoretical exploration of computational complexity classes (P, NP, NP-complete, and PSPACE).

source_coverage.coverage_comment: Comprehensive syllabus provided, clearly detailing course objectives, topics, laboratory works, prerequisites, and evaluation criteria.

theoretical_understanding: Understand the mathematical foundations of algorithmic complexity and asymptotic notations
Differentiate between complexity classes such as P, NP, NP-complete, and PSPACE
Comprehend the principles of recurrence relations and their proofs (Master Theorem)
practical_implementation: Implement advanced data structures including hash tables, priority queues, binary search trees, and red-black trees
Code sorting algorithms tailored for specific time constraints, such as quicksort, merge sort, and radix sort
Develop programmatic solutions leveraging greedy algorithms and dynamic programming paradigms
analysis_validation: Analyze the time and space complexity of computational algorithms mathematically
Validate the correctness and optimal substructure of dynamic programming algorithms
architecture_design: Select appropriate algorithms and data structures based on the constraints of a given computational problem
Model real-world scenarios as graph or scheduling problems to apply algorithmic strategies
research_and_prototyping: Reduce theoretical problems to prove NP-completeness (e.g., 3-SAT to Hamiltonian Cycle)

implementation_tasks: Implementing and comparing internal sorting methods
Solving optimization tasks using dynamic programming and greedy strategies
engineering_practices: Code testing and defense against edge cases

curricular_relations.reason: Understanding asymptotic notation and recurrence relations is necessary to formally evaluate sorting algorithms like Merge Sort and Quicksort.
Proficiency in basic programming is required to implement complex linked data structures like trees.
Understanding optimization algorithms lays the practical groundwork for studying NP-hard optimization problems and complexity bounds.

what_student_can_understand: How to mathematically prove the efficiency of an algorithm and determine its lower limits.
The theoretical boundaries of computation and why certain problems (NP-hard) cannot be solved quickly.
How different underlying data structures impact the performance of software applications.
what_student_can_build: Custom, highly-optimized data structures like Hash Tables and Red-Black Trees.
Programs that efficiently sort and search through massive datasets.
Graph-based models to represent and traverse complex networks.
what_student_can_apply: Dynamic programming techniques to break down and solve multi-stage decision processes.
Greedy algorithms for real-time scheduling and resource allocation optimization.
